newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk president warns Islamist premier in letter.
newsitem.headline: Turk president warns Islamist premier in letter.

text.p: Turkey's president has sent a letter to Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, expressing his concern the Islamist-led government was increasingly at odds with the officially secular system, newspapers said on Thursday.

"There is a widespread feeling that you are diverting from the secularist, democratic republican aims. This is also my belief," the mass-selling Hurriyet daily quoted President Suleyman Demirel as saying in the letter.
"If you continue with this attitude the regime will be in danger," Demirel wrote to Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader.

The letter, reported in some other newspapers, was also copied to armed forces leader Ismail Hakki Karadayi on the eve of a crucial meeting later this week between top politicians and the restive chiefs of the secularist armed forces.

The armed forces have warned Erbakan's Islamist-right coalition in recent weeks against increasing the role of Islam in public life, and these issues are expected to be discussed at Friday's meeting of the National Security Council.
Opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz on Wednesday called for an alliance of all parties except Erbakan's Welfare Party to evade the danger of the military staging a fourth coup since 1960.
Demirel, himself dislodged as premier during two of the three previous coups, warned Erbakan against the consequences of upsetting the army and other groups.
"You cannot tell what consequences this might bring," Demirel said. "Today the army, the universities and the street are all uneasy. You must desist from moves that could perpetuate this unease."
Many Turks have been taking part in a nightly protest that originally began as a demonstration against corruption but has recently taken a distinctly anti-Islamist turn.
Demirel told Erbakan in the letter quoted by Hurriyet that he would not approve any law that went against the principles of a secular, democratic republic.
